requirements.text: The central trading system (CTS) is to complete the trading of stock.
The CTS receive instructions from trade client serve.
The CTS produce new messages which to be sent to network message promulgating after deal with the instructions from trade client serve.
The system manager is authorization to access the information in CTS.
The CTS shall identify the kind of the instructions.
The CTS shall freeze the fund of user’s account according to the trade instruction.
The CTS shall support buy instruction with five parameters: user ID, stock ID, quantity, respected price, timestamp.
The CTS shall support sell instruction with five parameters: user ID, stock ID, quantity, respected price, timestamp.
The CTS shall support user query instruction with three parameters: user ID, query content, some restrict parameters.
The CTS shall support stock query instruction with three parameters: stock ID, query content, some restrict parameter.
The CTS shall match trading instructions based on price first principle and the time first principle.
The CTS shall reject trading instructions if the trading price is higher than the rising limit or lower than the falling limit.
The CTS shall return the trading result to the client serve.
The CTS shall remove instructions that have not finished trading in one day.
The CTS shall implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to restrict system manager access to specific administrative functions and maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions.

All data transmissions between the CTS and external subsystems shall be encrypted using TLS 1.3 or higher, and all incoming instructions must be validated against strict schema and business logic constraints to prevent injection attacks.
The CTS shall implement atomic transaction handling for fund freezing to ensure data integrity, preventing race conditions where the same funds could be committed to multiple trades.
The CTS shall process at least 5,000 trade instructions per second with a maximum end-to-end latency of 50ms under peak load.
The system shall maintain 99.99% availability and ensure a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of less than 30 seconds in the event of a component failure.
The system shall log all transaction attempts, failures, and system exceptions to a persistent, immutable audit store for reconciliation purposes.
All inter-subsystem communications shall be encrypted via TLS 1.3, and all access to the CTS shall be authenticated and authorized via a centralized identity provider.
The CTS shall process buy/sell instructions with a P99 latency of less than 50ms and support a throughput of at least 10,000 transactions per second.
The system shall support a concurrent load of 50,000 active users and maintain an order book capacity of at least 1,000,000 open instructions.
The CTS shall return the trading result to the client service within 100ms of the matching event.
